akhfash:15-15.t: He said ﴿بِأَيْدِي سَفَرَةٍ﴾: their singular is "السافِر", like "الكافِر" and "الكَفَرة".

akhfash:16-16.t: And He said ﴿كِرَامٍ بَرَرَةٍ﴾: their singular is "البارّ", and "البَرَرة" is a plural (in the meaning) of "الأَبْرار".

akhfash:17-17.t: And He said ﴿قُتِلَ ٱلإِنسَانُ مَآ أَكْفَرَهُ﴾: its meaning is on two aspects: some said "as an exclamation of wonder (taʿajjub)", and some said: "what thing has made him disbelieve?" (أيُّ شَيْءٍ أَكْفَرَهُ).

akhfash:20-20.t: He said ﴿ثُمَّ ٱلسَّبِيلَ يَسَّرَهُ﴾: you say "الطريقَ هَدَاهُ" ("the road — He guided him"), that is: "He guided him to the road" (هداهُ الطريقَ).

daas-irab:1-4.t: ﴿عَبَسَ﴾: a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya) and has no grammatical position. ﴿وَتَوَلَّى﴾: a past verb whose agent is latent; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿أَنْ﴾: a maṣdar-forming particle that puts the verb in the accusative; ﴿جاءَهُ﴾: a past verb and its object; ﴿الْأَعْمى﴾: postponed agent; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from an and the verb is accusative by removal of the preposition. ﴿وَما يُدْرِيكَ﴾: an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject), and an imperfect verb and its first object, the agent being latent; ﴿لَعَلَّهُ﴾: laʿalla and its noun; ﴿يَزَّكَّى﴾: an imperfect verb whose agent is latent; the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of laʿalla, the clause لعل… is the second object of يدريك, the clause يدريك… is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ ما, and the clause ما يدريك is resumptive. ﴿أَوْ﴾: a conjunction; ﴿يَذَّكَّرُ﴾: conjoined to يزكي. ﴿فَتَنْفَعَهُ﴾: the fāʾ is causal (sababiyya), and an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by an implied an after the causal fāʾ; the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿الذِّكْرى﴾: agent.

daas-irab:5-10.t: ﴿أَمَّا﴾: a particle of condition and detailing; ﴿مَنِ﴾: a relative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿اسْتَغْنى﴾: a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of من. ﴿فَأَنْتَ﴾: the fāʾ is the linking fāʾ (rābiṭa) and ﴿أنت﴾ is mubtadaʾ; ﴿لَهُ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) what follows them; ﴿تَصَدَّى﴾: an imperfect verb whose agent is latent; the clause is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ أنت, the clause أنت… is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ من, and the clause من… is resumptive. ﴿وَما﴾: the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya) and ﴿ما﴾ is negative; ﴿عَلَيْكَ﴾: fronted khabar; ﴿أن﴾: a maṣdar-forming particle that puts the verb in the accusative; ﴿لا﴾: negative; ﴿يَزَّكَّى﴾: an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by an, its agent latent; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from an and the verb is the postponed mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿وَأَمَّا﴾: a particle of condition and detailing; ﴿مَنْ﴾: mubtadaʾ; ﴿جاءَكَ﴾: a past verb and its object, the agent being latent; the clause is the ṣila of من; ﴿يَسْعى﴾: an imperfect verb whose agent is latent; the clause is a ḥāl, and the clause أما من… is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَهُوَ﴾: the wāw is circumstantial and ﴿هُوَ﴾ is mubtadaʾ; ﴿يَخْشى﴾: an imperfect verb whose agent is latent; the verbal clause is the khabar and the nominal clause is a ḥāl. ﴿فَأَنْتَ عَنْهُ تَلَهَّى﴾: parsed like فأنت له تصدى.

daas-irab:11-16.t: ﴿كَلَّا﴾: a particle of deterrence and rebuke; ﴿إِنَّها﴾: inna and its noun; ﴿تَذْكِرَةٌ﴾: its khabar (predicate); the clause is resumptive. ﴿فَمَنْ﴾: the fāʾ is a resumptive particle and ﴿من﴾ is a conditional noun that puts the verb in the jussive, mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿شاءَ﴾: a past verb in the position of a jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir); ﴿ذَكَرَهُ﴾: a past verb in the position of a jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and the agent is latent; the clause is the apodosis and has no grammatical position, the two clauses of the condition and the apodosis are the khabar of the mubtadaʾ من, and the clause من… is resumptive. ﴿فِي صُحُفٍ﴾: naʿt (adjective) of تذكرة; ﴿مُكَرَّمَةٍ﴾: adjective of صحف; ﴿مَرْفُوعَةٍ مُطَهَّرَةٍ﴾: two adjectives of صحف; ﴿بِأَيْدِي﴾: also an adjective of صحف; ﴿سَفَرَةٍ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); ﴿كِرامٍ بَرَرَةٍ﴾: two adjectives of an omitted qualified noun, its implied form being "ملائكة" (angels).

daas-irab:17-23.t: ﴿قُتِلَ﴾: a passive past verb; ﴿الْإِنْسانُ﴾: nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position. ﴿ما﴾: a complete indefinite (nakira tāmma), mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿أَكْفَرَهُ﴾: a past verb and its object, the fāʿil (agent) being latent (mustatir); the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause is resumptive. ﴿مِنْ أَيِّ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb after them; ﴿شَيْءٍ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); ﴿خَلَقَهُ﴾: a past verb and its object, the agent being latent; the clause is resumptive. ﴿مِنْ نُطْفَةٍ﴾: attached to what follows them; ﴿خَلَقَهُ﴾: a past verb and its object, the agent being latent; the clause is a badal (substitute) for the preceding one; ﴿فَقَدَّرَهُ﴾: conjoined to خلقه by the fāʾ. ﴿ثُمَّ﴾: a conjunction; ﴿السَّبِيلَ﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an omitted verb explained by the one mentioned after it; ﴿يَسَّرَهُ﴾: an imperfect verb [Translator's note: so in the source; يسّر is a past verb] and its object, the agent being latent; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿ثُمَّ أَماتَهُ فَأَقْبَرَهُ﴾: conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿ثُمَّ﴾: a conjunction; ﴿إِذا﴾: a conditional adverb that does not put the verb in the jussive; ﴿شاءَ﴾: a past verb whose agent is latent; the clause is in the position of a genitive by annexation (iḍāfa); ﴿أَنْشَرَهُ﴾: a past verb and its object, the agent being latent; the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) and has no grammatical position. ﴿كَلَّا﴾: a particle of deterrence and rebuke; ﴿لَمَّا يَقْضِ﴾: an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by lammā, the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the weak letter from its end, the agent being latent; ﴿ما﴾: direct object; ﴿أَمَرَهُ﴾: a past verb and its object, the agent being latent; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of ما, and the clause كلا… is resumptive and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:24-26.t: ﴿فَلْيَنْظُرِ﴾: the fāʾ is a resumptive particle, and an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by the lām of command; ﴿الْإِنْسانُ﴾: fāʿil (agent); ﴿إِلى طَعامِهِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; the clause is resumptive. ﴿أَنَّا صَبَبْنَا﴾: anna and its noun, and a past verb and its agent; ﴿الْماءَ﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿صَبًّا﴾: mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); the clause is the khabar (predicate) of anna, and the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from anna and what follows it is a badal of inclusion (badal ishtimāl, a substitute) for طعامه. ﴿ثُمَّ﴾: a conjunction; ﴿شَقَقْنَا الْأَرْضَ شَقًّا﴾: conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:27-32.t: ﴿فَأَنْبَتْنا﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); ﴿فِيها﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; ﴿حَبًّا﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَعِنَباً وَقَضْباً وَزَيْتُوناً وَنَخْلًا﴾: conjoined to what precedes them. ﴿وَحَدائِقَ﴾: also conjoined; ﴿غُلْباً﴾: naʿt (adjective) of حدائق. ﴿وَفاكِهَةً وَأَبًّا﴾: conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿مَتاعاً﴾: mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), accusative (manṣūb); ﴿لَكُمْ﴾: attached to متاعا; ﴿وَلِأَنْعامِكُمْ﴾: conjoined to what precedes them.

daas-irab:33-37.t: ﴿فَإِذا﴾: the fāʾ is a resumptive particle and ﴿إذا﴾ is a conditional adverb that does not put the verb in the jussive; ﴿جاءَتِ الصَّاخَّةُ﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is in the position of a genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿يَوْمَ﴾: an adverb of time, badal (substitute) for إذا; ﴿يَفِرُّ الْمَرْءُ﴾: an imperfect verb and its agent; the clause is in the position of a genitive by annexation; ﴿مِنْ أَخِيهِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) what precedes them; ﴿وَأُمِّهِ وَأَبِيهِ﴾: conjoined to what precedes them; ﴿وَصاحِبَتِهِ وَبَنِيهِ﴾: also conjoined. ﴿لِكُلِّ﴾: attached to an omitted fronted khabar (predicate); ﴿امْرِئٍ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); ﴿مِنْهُمْ﴾: naʿt (adjective) of امرئ; ﴿يَوْمَئِذٍ﴾: an adverb of time annexed to one like it; ﴿شَأْنٌ﴾: postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿يُغْنِيهِ﴾: an imperfect verb and its object, the agent being latent (mustatir); the verbal clause is an adjective of شأن, and the nominal clause لكل امرئ… is resumptive and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:38-42.t: ﴿وُجُوهٌ﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿يَوْمَئِذٍ﴾: an adverb of time annexed to one like it; ﴿مُسْفِرَةٌ﴾: khabar (predicate); ﴿ضاحِكَةٌ مُسْتَبْشِرَةٌ﴾: two further predicates of وجوه; the nominal clause is resumptive. ﴿وَوُجُوهٌ﴾: mubtadaʾ; ﴿يَوْمَئِذٍ﴾: an adverb of time annexed to one like it; ﴿عَلَيْها﴾: fronted khabar; ﴿غَبَرَةٌ﴾: postponed mubtadaʾ; the clause is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, and the clause وجوه… is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿تَرْهَقُها﴾: an imperfect verb and its object; ﴿قَتَرَةٌ﴾: fāʿil (agent); the verbal clause is a second khabar of وجوه. ﴿أُولئِكَ﴾: mubtadaʾ; ﴿هُمُ﴾: a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl); ﴿الْكَفَرَةُ الْفَجَرَةُ﴾: two predicates; the clause is resumptive.

farraa:1-2.t: [126/a] His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿عَبَسَ وَتَوَلَّىٰ أَن جَآءَهُ ٱلأَعْمَىٰ﴾. That was ʿAbdullāh ibn Umm Maktūm — Umm Maktūm was his father's mother. He came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while there was with him a group of the nobles of Quraysh, to ask about something from which he would benefit; and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ disliked that he should interrupt his talk. So Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, sent down: ﴿عَبَسَ وَتَوَلَّىٰ﴾, meaning Muhammad ﷺ, ﴿أَن جَآءَهُ ٱلأَعْمَىٰ﴾: because the blind man came to him.

farraa:3-4.t:
Then He, Majestic and Mighty is He, said: ﴿وَمَا يُدْرِيكَ لَعَلَّهُ يَزَّكَّىٰ﴾.
By what he wanted to learn of your knowledge. Then the Prophet ﷺ turned with kindness to Ibn Umm Maktūm [«على أن ابن أم مكتوم» in the source — Translator's note: «أن» appears to be an intrusion], and honoured him after this verse, to the point that he appointed him as his deputy to lead the prayer. The readers agreed on: ﴿فَتَنفَعَهُ ٱلذِّكْرَىٰ﴾ with the nominative [Translator's note: so in the source, although the vowelled quotation shows the accusative فتنفعَه; the readings are reported the other way round elsewhere]; if it were accusative as the response of the fāʾ to لعلّ, it would be correct.
Someone recited to me:
علَّ صروفَ الدَّهر أو دولاتِها * يُدلْنَنَا اللَّمَّة من لَمّاتها
فتستريحَ النفس من زفْراتها * وتُنْقعَ الغلَّةُ من غُلاتها
(Perhaps the vicissitudes of time or its turns will grant us a turn from among its turns, so that the soul may rest from its sighs and the burning thirst be quenched.)
Some read: "أأن جاءه الأعمى" with two hamzas with fatḥa, i.e.: because the blind man came to him he frowned; and it is like His saying: "أأنْ كان ذا مالٍ وبَنِينَ".

farraa:6-6.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَأَنتَ لَهُ تَصَدَّىٰ﴾.
If a reader read: "تَصَدّى" [Translator's note: so in the source; presumably the passive تُصَدَّى is meant], it would be correct.

farraa:11-13.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿كَلاَّ إِنَّهَا تَذْكِرَةٌ﴾.
This sura is a reminder. If you wish, you make the hāʾ a support (ʿimād) because of the feminine of التذكرة.
﴿فَمَن شَآءَ ذَكَرَهُ﴾:
he remembers the Qur'an; the masculine [pronoun] goes back to the revelation.
﴿فَي صُحُفٍ مُّكَرَّمَةٍ﴾:
because they came down from the Preserved Tablet, raised high with your Lord there, purified; none touches them but the purified. This is like His saying: ﴿فَالْمُدَبِّرَاتِ أَمْراً﴾.
He made [126/b] the angels and the scrolls purified, because purification applies to the scrolls, so He made purification belong to those who carry them as well.

farraa:15-15.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿بِأَيْدِي سَفَرَةٍ﴾.
They are the angels; the singular is سافر. The Arabs say: سفرت بين القوم (I mediated between the people) when you make peace between them. So the angels, when they descend with the revelation of Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, and His instruction, were made like the envoy (السفير) who makes peace between people. The poet said:
وما أدعُ السِّفارةَ بينَ قومى * وما أمْشى بغشٍّ إن مَشَيْتُ
(I do not abandon mediation among my people, and I do not go about with deceit when I go.)
And البررة: its singular, by analogy in Arabic, is بارّ; because the Arabs do not say فَعَلة intending a plural unless its singular is فاعل, like كافر and كفرة, and فاجر and فجرة. This is the rule, by which its singular is بارّ. What the Arabs [actually] say is: رجل بَرّ (a pious man) and امرأة برّة (a pious woman); then it was given a plural on the interpretation of فاعل, as they said: قوم خَيَرَة بَرَرَة (good, pious people) — I heard it from one of the Arabs — and the singular of الخيرة is خيّر, and of البررة: برّ. Similar to it is: قوم سَراة (noble people), whose singular is سَرِيّ; it ought to have been سارٍ. When the Arabs pluralise سارٍ they pluralise it with a ḍamma on the first letter and say: سُراة and غُزاة. So it is as though, when they said سَراة, they disliked giving its first letter a ḍamma, which would make the singular seem to be سارٍ; so they wanted to distinguish, by the fatḥa on the first letter of سَراة, between السريّ and الساري.

farraa:17-19.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿مَآ أَكْفَرَهُ﴾.
It may be an exclamation of wonder, and it may be: what is it that made him disbelieve? The exegesis came with this second interpretation. Then He made him wonder and said: ﴿مِنْ أَيِّ شَيءٍ خَلَقَهُ﴾. Then [127/a] He explained and said: ﴿مِن نُّطْفَةٍ خَلَقَهُ فَقَدَّرَهُ﴾ — in stages: a drop, then a clot, to the end of his creation; and wretched or happy, and male or female.

farraa:20-20.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ثُمَّ ٱلسَّبِيلَ يَسَّرَهُ﴾.
Its meaning: then He made him at ease with the way (يسّره للسبيل). Similar to it is: ﴿إِنَّا هَدَيْنَاهُ السَّبِيلَ﴾, i.e. We made known to him the way of good and the way of evil.

farraa:21-21.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ثُمَّ أَمَاتَهُ فَأَقْبَرَهُ﴾.
He made him one who is buried, and did not make him one of those thrown to the beasts of prey and the birds, nor one of those placed in ossuaries (النواويس); as though the grave is one of the things by which the Muslim was honoured. He did not say فقبره, because القابر is the one who buries with his hand, while المُقبِر is Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, because He made him one who has a grave; and His act is not like the act of the human (الآمى) [Translator's note: so in the source; read الآدمي]. The Arabs say: بترتُ ذنب البعير (I cut off the camel's tail), and والله أبتره (and Allah made it tailless).
And عضبت قرن الثور (I broke the bull's horn), and والله أعضبه (Allah made it broken-horned); and طردت فلاناً عني (I drove So-and-so away from me), and والله أطرده, i.e. He made him an outcast. If someone said فقبره, or said of a human أقبره when he directs it in his sense, it would be acceptable and correct. Do you not see that you say: "So-and-so killed his brother", and another says: "Allah killed him"? The Arabs say: هذه كلمة مُقتِلة مُخيفة (this is a word that gets one killed, that brings fear) when whoever says it would be killed; it is said thus, and if one said of it قاتلة خائفة, it would be correct, as you say: هذا الداء قاتلك (this disease is killing you).

farraa:23-23.t:
His saying, Blessed and Exalted is He: ﴿كَلاَّ لَمَّا يَقْضِ مَآ أَمَرَهُ﴾.
He has not fulfilled some of what He commanded him.

farraa:25-25.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَنَّا صَبَبْنَا ٱلْمَآءَ صَبّاً﴾.
Al-Aʿmash and ʿĀṣim read (أنّا), making it in the position of the genitive, i.e.: let him look at Our pouring the water, [i.e.] to [the fact] that We poured, and did such and such. The people of the Hijaz and al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī read (إنّا), giving information about the description of the food by way of resumption (istiʾnāf); and both are good. Likewise His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿فَانْظُرْ كَيْفَ كَانَ عَاقبةُ مَكْرِهِمْ أَنَّا دَمَّرْنَاهُمْ﴾ and ﴿إِنا دمرناهم﴾. The position of "أنّا" here in (ʿAbasa), when it has a fatḥa, may also be nominative, as though He resumed and said: his food is Our pouring the water and Our causing such and such to grow.

farraa:27-27.t:
His saying, Blessed and Exalted is He: ﴿حَبّاً﴾.
الحب: all grains — wheat, barley and what is besides them. القضب: fresh fodder (الرطبة); the people of Mecca call fodder (القتّ) القضب. الحدائق: every garden that has a wall around it is a حديقة; what has no wall around it is not called حديقة. الغُلْب: what is thick among the palm trees. الأبّ: what the livestock eat. That is what Ibn ʿAbbās said.

farraa:32-32.t:
His saying, Blessed and Exalted is He: ﴿مَّتَاعاً لَّكُمْ﴾.
That is: We created it as an enjoyment for you and a benefit. If it were nominative, it would be permissible, as we have explained.

farraa:33-33.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ٱلصَّآخَّةُ﴾: the Resurrection.

farraa:34-34.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يَوْمَ يَفِرُّ ٱلْمَرْءُ مِنْ أَخِيهِ﴾.
He flees from his brother: من and عن are the same in it.

farraa:37-37.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لِكُلِّ ٱمْرِىءٍ مِّنْهُمْ يَوْمَئِذٍ شَأْنٌ يُغْنِيهِ﴾.
That is: it occupies him away from his kin. One of the readers read: "يعنيه" (concerns him), and that is anomalous (shādhdh).

farraa:38-38.t:
His saying, Blessed and Exalted is He: ﴿وُجُوهٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ مُّسْفِرَةٌ﴾.
Shining, bright. When a woman casts off her veil or her face-cover, it is said: سفرت, so she is سافر; and one does not say أسفرت.

farraa:41-41.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿تَرْهَقُهَا قَتَرَةٌ﴾.
In speech, قَتْرة, with the tāʾ vowelless, is permissible; but no one has read it so.

zajjaj:1-2.t:
Sūrat ʿAbasa
Meccan
﷽
His saying: ﴿عَبَسَ وتَوَلّى﴾ ﴿أنْ جاءَهُ الأعْمى﴾: «أنْ» is in the position of the accusative as a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose); the meaning is: "because the blind man came to him." These verses and those after them, up to His saying ﴿فَأنْتَ عَنْهُ تَلَهّى﴾ [ʿAbasa: 10], were revealed concerning ʿAbd Allāh ibn Umm Maktūm. He had come to the Prophet ﷺ while the Prophet was calling one of the nobles of Quraysh to Islam, hoping that others would embrace Islam through his embracing it; so he, upon him be peace, was occupied with calling him and did not turn to ʿAbd Allāh ibn Umm Maktūm. So Allah commanded him not to be occupied with anyone else so as not to turn to any one of the Muslims, and said: ﴿عَبَسَ وتَوَلّى﴾ ﴿أنْ جاءَهُ الأعْمى﴾ ﴿وَما يُدْرِيكَ لَعَلَّهُ يَزَّكّى﴾ [ʿAbasa: 3] ﴿أوْ يَذَّكَّرُ فَتَنْفَعَهُ الذِّكْرى﴾ [ʿAbasa: 4]. It is also read «فَتَنْفَعُهُ الذِّكْرى». Whoever reads it in the accusative does so as the answer to «لَعَلَّ», and whoever reads it in the nominative does so by conjunction with «يَزَّكّى».

zajjaj:5-6.t: His saying: ﴿أمّا مَنِ اسْتَغْنى﴾ ﴿فَأنْتَ لَهُ تَصَدّى﴾, that is: you turn towards him. It is also read «تَصَّدّى». Whoever read ﴿تَصَدّى﴾ with the ṣād undoubled — the origin is «تَتَصَدّى», but the second tāʾ was dropped because two tāʾs came together. Whoever read «تَصَّدّى» with assimilation of the tāʾ — the meaning is also «تَتَصَدّى», except that the tāʾ was assimilated into the ṣād because the two points of articulation are close, the articulation of the tāʾ to the ṣād.

zajjaj:7-7.t: His saying: ﴿وَما عَلَيْكَ ألا يَزَّكّى﴾, that is: what blame is upon you if the one you call to Islam does not embrace Islam?!

zajjaj:10-10.t: His saying: ﴿فَأنْتَ عَنْهُ تَلَهّى﴾: its meaning is "you are occupied (away from him)". One says «لَهَيْتُ عَنِ الشَّيْءِ، ألْهى عَنْهُ» when I am occupied away from it.

zajjaj:11-11.t: His saying: ﴿كَلا إنَّها تَذْكِرَةٌ﴾: by it is meant this admonition with which Allah admonished the Prophet, upon him be peace.

zajjaj:12-12.t: ﴿فَمَن شاءَ ذَكَرَهُ﴾: the pronoun is masculine because «اَلْمَوْعِظَةُ» (admonition, feminine) and «اَلْوَعْظُ» (admonishing, masculine) are one. The meaning refers back to the bearers of the Qur'an; the meaning is: "whoever wishes to remember it remembers it." Then He, Majestic and Mighty, informed that the Book is in the Preserved Tablet with Him, saying: ﴿فِي صُحُفٍ مُكَرَّمَةٍ﴾ [ʿAbasa: 13] ﴿مَرْفُوعَةٍ مُطَهَّرَةٍ﴾ [ʿAbasa: 14] ﴿بِأيْدِي سَفَرَةٍ﴾ [ʿAbasa: 15]. «اَلسَّفَرَةُ» are the scribes, meaning the angels; the singular is «سافِرٌ», plural «سَفَرَةٌ», like «كاتِبٌ» and «كَتَبَةٌ», «كافِرٌ» and «كَفَرَةٌ». The scribes were called «سَفَرَةٌ» and the scribe «سافِرٌ» only because its meaning is that he makes a thing clear and plain. One says «أسْفَرَ الصُّبْحُ» when the dawn shines, and «سَفَرَتِ المَرْأةُ» when the woman removes the veil from her face; and from it is «سَفَرْتُ بَيْنَ القَوْمِ» ("I mediated between the people"), that is: I laid bare the heart of this one and the heart of that one, in order to reconcile them.

zajjaj:17-17.t:
His saying: ﴿قُتِلَ الإنْسانُ ما أكْفَرَهُ﴾: it may be in the form of the wording of wonder (taʿajjub), the wonder being something the children of Adam are commanded to do.
The meaning would then be like His saying: ﴿فَما أصْبَرَهم عَلى النّارِ﴾ [al-Baqara: 175], that is: you should wonder at the unbelief of man. It may also be in the sense of rebuke, its wording being the wording of a question, that is: "What has made him disbelieve?!" Then He made clear about him that by which he ought to have known that Allah is his Creator and that He is One, saying: ﴿مِن أيِّ شَيْءٍ خَلَقَهُ﴾ [ʿAbasa: 18], in the wording of a question whose meaning is to make him acknowledge (taqrīr). Then He made it clear, saying: ﴿مِن نُطْفَةٍ خَلَقَهُ فَقَدَّرَهُ﴾ [ʿAbasa: 19]; the meaning is "and He proportioned him in due form", as He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿أكَفَرْتَ بِالَّذِي خَلَقَكَ مِن تُرابٍ ثُمَّ مِن نُطْفَةٍ ثُمَّ سَوّاكَ رَجُلا﴾ [al-Kahf: 37].

zajjaj:20-20.t: His saying: ﴿ثُمَّ السَّبِيلَ يَسَّرَهُ﴾, that is: He guided him to the way, whether grateful or ungrateful.

zajjaj:21-21.t:
His saying: ﴿ثُمَّ أماتَهُ فَأقْبَرَهُ﴾: the meaning of «أقْبَرَهُ» is: He provided him with a grave in which he is hidden. One says «أقْبَرْتُ فُلانًا» — I provided him with a grave — and «قَبَرْتُ فُلانًا» — I buried him, so I am his burier (qābir). The poet said:
؎لَوْ أسْنَدَتْ مَيْتًا إلى نَحْرِها ∗∗∗ عاشَ ولَمْ يُنْقَلْ إلى قابِرِ
(Were she to lean a dead man against her bosom, he would live and not be carried off to a burier.)

zajjaj:22-22.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿ثُمَّ إذا شاءَ أنْشَرَهُ﴾: its meaning is: He resurrects him. One says «أنْشَرَ اللَّهُ المَوْتى، فَنُشِرُوا» ("Allah raised the dead, and they were raised"), and the singular is «ناشِرٌ». The poet said:
؎حَتّى يَقُولَ النّاسُ مِمّا رَأوْا ∗∗∗ يا عَجَبًا لِلْمَيِّتِ النّاشِرِ
(Until people say, at what they have seen: how wondrous, the dead man risen!)

zajjaj:24-24.t: His saying: ﴿فَلْيَنْظُرِ الإنْسانُ إلى طَعامِهِ﴾, that is: let man look at how Allah created his food and the food of all animals, which Allah made a means of their life.

zajjaj:25-25.t:
﴿أنّا صَبَبْنا الماءَ صَبًّا﴾ — it is also read «إنّا صَبَبْنا». Whoever reads «إنّا» does so as a new beginning and resumption (istiʾnāf). Whoever reads «أنّا» does so as a badal (substitute) from the food, and «إنّا» is then in the position of the genitive; the meaning is: "let man look at (the fact) that We poured down water abundantly."
«[Translator's note: in the last clause the source prints «إنّا», though the reading under discussion is «أنّا».]»

zajjaj:26-26.t: ﴿ثُمَّ شَقَقْنا الأرْضَ شَقًّا﴾, that is: with the vegetation.

zajjaj:27-27.t: ﴿فَأنْبَتْنا فِيها حَبًّا﴾: «اَلْحَبُّ» is everything that is harvested, like wheat and barley and everything having grain that is used for nourishment. «اَلْقَضْبُ» is fresh fodder (al-ruṭaba).

zajjaj:30-30.t: ﴿وَحَدائِقَ غُلْبًا﴾: «حَدائِقَ», its singular is «حَدِيقَةٌ»; they are orchards and intertwined trees. His saying ﴿غُلْبًا﴾ means: dense and large.

zajjaj:31-31.t: ﴿وَفاكِهَةً وأبًّا﴾: «اَلْأبُّ» is all the pasture that livestock graze on. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, mentioned among His signs what points to His oneness in bringing into being what nourishes all animals.

zajjaj:32-32.t: His saying: ﴿مَتاعًا لَكم ولأنْعامِكُمْ﴾: it is accusative as an emphasising maṣdar (verbal noun) of His saying "so We caused to grow in it the things that were mentioned", because His causing these things to grow has given enjoyment through them to creation, people and all animals.

zajjaj:33-33.t: His saying: ﴿فَإذا جاءَتِ الصّاخَّةُ﴾: (the blast) upon which the Resurrection takes place; it deafens (taṣikhkhu) the ears, that is, makes them deaf, so that nothing is heard except that in which there is a call to bring them to life. Then He explained at what time it comes, saying: ﴿يَوْمَ يَفِرُّ المَرْءُ مِن أخِيهِ﴾ [ʿAbasa: 34] up to His saying: ﴿لِكُلِّ امْرِئٍ مِنهم يَوْمَئِذٍ شَأْنٌ يُغْنِيهِ﴾ [ʿAbasa: 37], with dotted ghayn. It has also been read «شَأْنٌ يُعْنِيهِ», that is: an affair along with which nothing else concerns him; and likewise «يُغْنِيهِ»: being preoccupied with it, he is not able to be preoccupied with anything else. Then He made clear the states of the believers and the unbelievers. He described the states of the believers, saying: ﴿وُجُوهٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ مُسْفِرَةٌ﴾ [ʿAbasa: 38] ﴿ضاحِكَةٌ مُسْتَبْشِرَةٌ﴾ [ʿAbasa: 39] — «مُسْفِرَةٌ» means shining, having known what triumph and bliss is theirs. And He described the unbelievers and the people of the Fire, saying: ﴿وَوُجُوهٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ عَلَيْها غَبَرَةٌ﴾ [ʿAbasa: 40] ﴿تَرْهَقُها قَتَرَةٌ﴾ [ʿAbasa: 41], that is: dust over which rises a blackness like smoke. Then He made clear who the people of this state are, saying: ﴿أُولَئِكَ هُمُ الكَفَرَةُ الفَجَرَةُ﴾ [ʿAbasa: 42].
